content.text:
━━━ 📃 SUMMARY ━━━ 7/7

🔄 ITERATION on: parent-selector closing the modal, then two more symptoms reported mid-investigation

📃 CONTENT:

**What I found: I could not reproduce any of the three symptoms in the code, and the evidence points to a stale browser session rather than an app bug.**

The investigation, honestly reported:
- I tried to reproduce in your real Chrome first (doctrine), but the Interceptor extension on the Mac would not connect after five attempts (daemon runs, "no extensions connected") — so live-browser evidence was unavailable and I fell back to code-level reproduction.
- **Select closing the modal**: the rendered-DOM probe shows closing a select inside the modal leaves the modal open and never fires its close handler. There is exactly one copy of the Radix layering module in the dependency graph (the known cause of this exact symptom when duplicated — it isn't).
- **Save opening a new tab**: there is no code path that can open a tab — no `window.open`, no `target="_blank"`, no forms outside sign-in; Save is a plain button with a click handler.

What *does* explain all three at once: your tab (or installed PWA window) has been open across today's **four deploys** (v1.13.1 → v1.16.0). A page running old JavaScript against the new server mixes build artefacts — that genuinely breaks Radix's portal layering (select-close dismisses the dialog, in every modal), and a failed chunk load falls back to a native navigation, which an installed PWA opens as a separate browser tab.

**What I shipped (v1.16.1, live):** version-skew protection so this class of problem announces itself. The health endpoint now reports the server's build version, and the app checks it on load, on window focus, and every 5 minutes — when the server is newer than the running page, a banner appears: "BudgetBuddy v1.16.1 is available — this window is running vX and may misbehave. **Reload**." Gate was green before deploy (454 tests, typecheck, lint).

**Your next step: hard-refresh the app (Ctrl+Shift+R, or close and reopen the PWA window) and retest the three behaviours.** If any of them still happens on a fresh v1.16.1 session, open DevTools (F12) → Console, and paste me the red errors — that pins it in one step. Getting the Mac's Interceptor extension reconnected would also let me drive the reproduction myself next time.

🖊️ STORY:
- Three UI ghosts reported across modals and saves
- Code and harness both refuse to reproduce them
- Diagnosis: stale session spanning four same-day deploys
- Shipped version-skew banner; hard refresh and retest

**Found it, fixed it, and repaired your Gym budget — v1.16.2 is live.**

The root cause: the engine stores every budget amount as its *monthly equivalent*, with the cadence (weekly/annual/etc.) kept as a label. The category-page editor and the edit-budget wizard both convert your typed figure before saving — but the main page's edit modal posted the raw number. The same bug sat in the modal's *create* path and in the adopt-category modal; all three now convert. I also made the edit modal seed its amount and cadence from the authoritative budget version once it loads, because the row figure it previously seeded from is prorated/range-summed and can disagree with the plan rate when you're viewing a multi-month range.

The fix is pinned by a test that walks your exact scenario: a $22-weekly budget seeds as 22.00/weekly and posts 9533 cents monthly-equivalent, never the raw 2200.

# Budget-history audit — BudgetBuddy vs PocketSmith (2026-08-12)

Read-only audit of every mapped category's budget chronology against PocketSmith's
budget events (1,695 events, 2023-07 → 2026-08). **19 categories match exactly;
26 diverge.** The divergences fall into five patterns, in descending priority.

## Pattern 1 — Flattened history (the Gym case): 18 categories, REPAIRABLE

Root cause: the legacy-start backfill gave open-since-forever lines a real *start
date* (2023-07-01) but kept their **current amount across the whole span**, so
every historical PocketSmith rate change was flattened into one era. This is
exactly "Gym shows only one historical budget".

| Category | PocketSmith says | BudgetBuddy has |
|---|---|---|
| Gym | 216.67 → 238.33 → 307.67 → 719.33 (Mar-26) → 433.33 | flat 433.33 |
| Phone | 112 → 130 → 160 | flat 160 |
| Health Insurance | 105.85 → 110 → 115 | flat 115 |
| Tolls | 100 → 50 → 20 | flat 20 |
| Water | 30 → 75 (Apr-26) | flat 75 |
| Spotify | 20 → 13.99 | flat 13.99 |
| Dog Food | 160 → 50 (Mar-26) | flat 50 |
| Doggy Day Care | 238.33 → 162.50 → 75 | flat 75 |
| Presents | 95 → 60 (Mar-26) | flat 60 |
| Shopping | 204 → 160 (Mar-26) | flat 160 |
| Recreation | 480 → 600 (Apr-26) | flat 600 |
| Healthcare | 300 → 150 → 220 | flat 220 |
| Internet | 70 → 93 (Apr-26) | flat 93 |
| Mortgage | 3185 → 3318.71 → 3185 | flat 3185 |
| Electricity | 66 → 77 | flat 77 |
| Car Insurance | 194.33 (May-24 only) → 129.54 | flat 129.54 |
| Car Rego | 75 → 77.56 | flat 77.56 (plus BB-authored 37.81 from Aug-26) |
| Groceries | 500.09 → 499.92 → 505.92 | flat 505.92 (plus BB-authored 600 from Aug-26) |
| Public Transport | 173.33 (Feb-25→Feb-26), none since Mar-26 | flat 20 — **amounts disagree entirely; needs your eyes** |

Repair: split each flat span into the PocketSmith eras, **preserving every
BudgetBuddy-authored version** (Aug-26 changes like Groceries 600, Fuel 100,
Car Rego 37.81, Gym 95.33 stay untouched). Past months then recompute (D4).
Public Transport is excluded from auto-repair — PS says $173.33 where BB says
$20; one of them was never real.

## Pattern 2 — August 2026 "divergences" that are DELIBERATE: no action

Fuel (PS 200 vs BB 100), Car Rego (77.56 vs 37.81), Groceries (505.92 vs 600),
Gym (433.33 vs 95.33): these are your own BudgetBuddy edits this month.
BudgetBuddy is the system of record going forward; PocketSmith simply hasn't
been told. Not defects.

## Pattern 3 — Annual-cadence gaps in PocketSmith: no action

MCC Membership, Microsoft 365 (and the annual set generally) show "PS none"
months between yearly occurrences — an artefact of how PocketSmith represents
annual repeats, not missing budgets. BudgetBuddy's continuous monthly-equivalent
line is the correct amortised view.

## Pattern 4 — Income rows: MATCH once resolved correctly, but one real problem

The audit script day-weighted income (an artefact); resolved by expected day:

- **Salary: MATCHES.** Full chronology imported (6363.61 / 6269.21 / 7323.26 /
  7454.60). August resolves 7454.60 = PocketSmith. The 9,963 line you authored
  starts 3 Aug and rules from September. ✓
- **Rental: REAL PROBLEM.** The 1,170 line ends 31 Jul and your new line starts
  12 Aug — **1..11 Aug is a window gap**, and with the expected day inside it,
  August's expected rental income resolves to **$0**. Also the new line is
  **$750/week ($3,250/month equivalent)** — nearly triple the old $1,170/month.
  If that was an experiment during today's session, it should probably be
  deleted (the new delete button covers this) and the 1,170 line reopened; if
  the rent genuinely changed, the line needs its start pulled back to cover
  August's expected day.

## Pattern 5 — Concurrent PocketSmith series: 2 categories, judgement calls

- **Savings**: two identical concurrent $1,500/mo series (2023-07→2024-07) in
  PS; BudgetBuddy has NO budget lines at all. If Savings should carry that
  history, one $1,500 era can be imported; the duplicate is PS-side noise.
- **Gas**: concurrent $60 + $65 series over the same span; BB kept flat $65.
  Ambiguous — PS was double-budgeting gas that year.

## Recommended actions (awaiting approval)

1. **Auto-repair the 18 Pattern-1 categories**: split flat spans into PS eras,
   BB-authored versions preserved, D4 recompute, backup first.
2. **Rental**: tell me whether $750/week is real. Either way the August gap
   needs closing (reopen 1,170 through 11 Aug at minimum).
3. **Public Transport, Savings, Gas**: your call per the notes above.

Full month-by-month divergence detail: `~/.claude/jobs/cb80c131/tmp/audit-report.txt`
(regenerable read-only via the audit script).
